findings.title: ASN.1 decoder length accounting breaks with long-form lengths and does not validate bounds
Adding abstract `order()` to the public CryptoProvider interface breaks external implementations, and the new provider is selected silently
Leftover dead code and misleading name in AuthzClientCryptoProvider

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: ASN.1 decoder length accounting breaks with long-form lengths and does not validate bounds

Affected:
- authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:49-63
- authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:76-83
- authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:160-163

Explanation:
`readSequence` loops while `length > 0`. `readNext` can return `-1` for an indefinite length, which makes `new byte[length]` throw a NegativeArraySizeException (an unchecked exception) on malformed input. If an inner element claims more bytes than remain, the decoder throws a generic EOF IOException, so this part is acceptable. However, `readLength` rejects any long-form length `>= limit`. A DER signature fed to the decoder is bounded by the sequence length, so the check is acceptable. A zero-length element would make `length` never decrease, but `readNext` always returns at least 2 bytes, so there is no infinite loop. The real problem is the indefinite length: `readNext` computes `length = -1 + reset()` and then calls `read(length)`. This can produce a negative or wrong size and an unchecked exception. Untrusted signature input should only ever fail with an IOException.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
int length = readLength();
if (length < 0) throw new IOException("Indefinite length not supported");
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Adding abstract `order()` to the public CryptoProvider interface breaks external implementations, and the new provider is selected silently

Affected:
- common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:39-44
- common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:54-72

Explanation:
`order()` is a new abstract method with no default. Any third-party CryptoProvider will fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError. Giving it a default value, such as 100, is safer. The duplicate-provider check was also removed entirely. Conflicting providers with equal order (for example default and fips on the classpath together) now get resolved arbitrarily instead of failing fast. The "ignored providers" message is logged only at debug level, so a misconfiguration is hard to notice. Consider failing, or at least warning, when the top two providers have equal order.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
default int order() { return 100; }
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Leftover dead code and misleading name in AuthzClientCryptoProvider

Affected:
- authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:60-67
- authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:114-115

Explanation:
Lines 114-115 encode the values and discard the results, which is pointless work. `getBouncyCastleProvider` returns the default keystore's JDK provider, not BouncyCastle, which is misleading to callers. `getKeyStore` uses `format.name()` where other providers use `toString()`, which could yield a different type string.

Proposed fix:
Remove the two discarded `ASN1Encoder` calls. Document or rename the `getBouncyCastleProvider` behavior, and use `format.toString()` in `getKeyStore`.
